speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what are the plans to provide student care centres (SCCs) in Yishun South, including preschool centres; (b) what are the minimum criteria for private SCCs' operations to ensure that they provide acceptable standards of service; and (c) how often does the Ministry visit these centres to ensure compliance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: About a third are within the existing Nee Soon South ward at Yishun South.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Two of them are located in primary schools and the other two in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In recent years, the Ministry of Education (MOE) has steadily increased the number of school-based SCCs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF and MOE will continue to monitor the demand for SCC places and expand capacity where there is demand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: SCCs that wish to administer SCFA are required to register with MSF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF requires registered SCCs, including centres operated by private entities, to meet stipulated standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These include standards on, among other things, providing a clean and safe physical environment with appropriately sized activity areas, observing good safety, health and hygiene practices, proper supervision of students, and a structured daily programme that supports learning and development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: More frequent checks may be conducted as needed, for example, to look into feedback and complaints received and where the SCC has weaknesses identified in previous audits.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First, the feedback from my residents is that for the school-based SCCs, most of the time, my residents are told that the places are reserved for children from lower-income families.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many of those from middle-income families find that they have problems getting into school-based SCCs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Second, I am glad to hear that there is such a requirement of three square metres per student.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The feedback is that it is always very cramped.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They have visited the private ones, and they say that these are always very cramped, and the children, some lie on the floor, some lie on the table, and they look like they are not very well-run.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Third, the feedback received from private operators is that the Housing and Development Board (HDB) releases void deck space more for childcare centres, not so much for student care operators.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is there a plan for HDB to release void deck space to private operators for SCCs?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The last question is I understand that MOE has plans for after-school care in every primary school.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As it is today, the capacity in the Nee Soon South area, in particular, exceeds utilisation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If the Member has any requests or demands from any resident from her constituency, she may like to work with us to see how we can help.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As for the question about three square metres, we do have audit checks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have a framework where we work not only with operators, but also with parents, and whenever we know there are some inconsistencies in the practices, we will be more than happy to look at it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to make sure that the child's time in the SCC is meaningful and has value-add, and that helps in the educational journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For the question about the private sector, we take note of this feedback.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, we work with the local community and the agencies to see how we are able to meet the demand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At this point in time, in Nee Soon South, the demand is less than the capacity that we have.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will continue to see how we can facilitate this whole process of providing every child a good start in life.
